reviews.reasons: The opening is sound but the ledger does not settle inside the window. The plan's why says 'settled by day 14', yet the cash line books all 14 sales on day 12 with settlesDay 15 and proofDay is 15, one day past the 14-day window. Money must settle in the window, so the ledger as written misses the proof condition. The fix is in the plan's own evidence: sales accrue daily at ~37 visitors x 4% = ~1.5/day, and only sales closed by day 11 settle (3 days) by day 14. $500 / $39 = 12.8, so 13 sales ($507 gross, $481 after $2 costs - note: the target is settled cash collected, $507 >= $500) are needed; days 1-11 give ~407 visitors x 4% = ~16 expected sales. Rebook receipts as daily/weekly tranches each settling 3 days after sale, all by day 14, and cut the count to what settles. Everything else recomputes: price $39 is 44 paid orders on this listing (real price from this buyer population); conversion 44/1100 = 4% measured on this listing; cost $2 < $39; exposure $0 against a $0 capital limit; Brain produces the spreadsheet (PRODUCE_SPREADSHEET proved). Exclusions are right: reupholstery has no fulfiller on its card; foam inserts cost $48 vs $45 price.
findings: SETTLES_IN_TIME (ledger): proofDay 15 and receipt settlesDay 15 versus windowDays 14; the why's 'settled by day 14' contradicts the plan's own cash lines.
Schedule models 14 sales closing at once on day 11; at a steady ~1.5 sales/day the right model is continuous sales, which is what makes the window work.

Headroom is thin: expected ~16 sales by day 11 against 13 needed; at Poisson variance roughly a 1-in-5 chance of falling short, so state the shortfall test (e.g. fewer than 6 sales by day 5) rather than presenting 14 as certain.

Cost timing: delivery on day 12 precedes settlement; the $2/sale must come out of proceeds as stated since the contract allows $0 capital - the ledger's day-15 SPEND should be tied to the receipt it is paid from.

Brain's own MARKET_VOLUME basis reads '1100 visitors a day ... 15400 in 14 days'; the card says 1,100 per 30 days (~37/day). The plan correctly uses 37/day; do not rely on Brain's 15,400 figure. The author's disagreements about Brain's merged link bases for the two excluded openings are correct.

reviews.reasons: My settlement finding is resolved: sales are modelled as three continuous tranches (days 1-4, 5-8, 9-11) settling 3 days later on days 7, 11 and 14, proofDay 14, inside the 14-day window. Recomputed: 5 + 4 + 4 = 13 sales x $39 = $507 settled >= $500 (12 would be $468, so 13 is the minimum); expected ~148 + 148 + 111 = ~407 visitors x 4% = ~16 sales by day 11, each tranche counting fewer than expected (5 vs ~6, 4 vs ~6, 4 vs ~4.4). Costs $26 are paid from each tranche's own settled proceeds, so cash never goes negative against the $0 capital limit. Price is 44 paid orders on this listing; conversion 44/1,100 measured on it; Brain produces the spreadsheet. The shortfall test (fewer than 5 by day 5, fewer than 9 by day 8) is stated. Exclusions and disagreements with Brain's merged link bases are correct.
findings: Margin is ~3 sales on a Poisson mean of ~16 (roughly a 1-in-5 chance of falling below 13): the owner should treat the day-5 and day-8 tests as real stop signals.
Tranche 3's settlement lands exactly on day 14, the last day of the window; any payout delay on the marketplace beyond 3 days pushes $156 out of the window.
